dispositions.method: The automatic families first printed in 1775 that reach 3 or more papers, long-running ones included, were split into single printed items (story_items.py --long-running, items.json: 838 items found on the pages, 354 in 4 or more papers by the finder's count), and again with the families of 1774 over the 1775 pages (items_from_1774.json: 77 items, 8 in 4 or more). Every item in 3 or more papers was compared by machine with every page and counted again by its opening; a sweep of seven-word sequences shared by 4 or more papers found 895 runs, and the runs no finder item covers were read. Counted item by item (452 entries), 441 items meet the bar (count_1775.md). The items printed by every paper that survives for their weeks by the count were counted again by their own words with phrase searches over all 1,286 pages in both transcriptions; the admitted and chosen items were read on every page.
dispositions.selection_rule: The thin-year rule (Y-THIN, as amended on 23 November 2026, the owner's choice B1): an item, counted by its own words, is eligible when it was printed by more than half of the newspapers that survive for its weeks (those with a surviving issue between its first and last printing, and at least in the three weeks from its first printing), and by at least 4; as in R-01, the eligible items printed by every newspaper that survives for their weeks are admitted, and the other eligible items are chosen to cover the months and the kinds of news, about as many stories as a standard year (about 20 to 35); one affair's items as in X-1800-01; digests are not admitted; sub-stories (C-01), private persons (R-04) and the list of items read and not admitted (R-03) as in every year. In 1775 5 to 7 papers survive for any item's weeks (6 for most of the year), so the bar is 4 papers for every item.
dispositions.paper_counting: 1775 has 7 catalogue series, which are 7 papers: the Connecticut Courant, Dunlap's Pennsylvania Packet, Gaine's New-York Gazette and Dixon and Hunter's Virginia Gazette run all year; the New-Hampshire Gazette survives in 39 issues, to 12 December; Purdie's Virginia Gazette from its first issue, 3 February; the Pennsylvania Journal for 27 December only. No 1775 issue has a corrected date; the release's map lists 2 misfiled RevX pages, on which no admitted printing stands.
